questions.text:

questions.text:
To: Harry
From: Mrs Kenton

sections.title: Part 2
sections.instr:
Questions 7-13
For each question, choose the correct answer.
How important are museums to you?
We asked three young people this question and this is what they told us.
sections.passage:
Chris
A lot of my friends think museums are boring but I love them. I prefer ones where they move things round regularly, and bring in new things to keep it interesting. I also like to have things to listen to as well as look at. I suppose I like museums because I'm really interested in history and art. We study these subjects at college, but I've actually found out a lot more about them from museums than from my textbooks.

Emily
I'm lucky because I live in New York, so there are lots of great museums for me to visit. One thing I've learnt is that you should never try to see a whole museum the first time you go. Just go to one or two rooms, and then return as often as you can to see the rest. For me, it's important that the people who work in the museum are pleasant, and happy to talk to me about the things in the exhibition. That makes a big difference.

Daniel
I don't go to museums much, except during my holidays in new cities. Then I make sure I spend at least a day going to the most famous ones. If it's a big museum and I don't have much time, I sometimes walk into a room and choose just five things to look at. I also take a tour if there is one, as I learn so much more from listening to the person showing us round than I do if I'm by myself.

questions.text: Who always visits museums when they travel?
questions.expl: [AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Daniel: "during my holidays in new cities. Then I make sure I spend at least a day going to the most famous ones."

questions.expl: [AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Emily: "Just go to one or two rooms, and then return as often as you can to see the rest."

questions.text: Who likes museums where the exhibitions often change?
questions.expl: [AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Chris: "I prefer ones where they move things round regularly, and bring in new things..."

questions.text: Who says that museums should have friendly staff?
questions.expl: [AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Emily: "it's important that the people who work in the museum are pleasant, and happy to talk to me..."

questions.text: Who says that they sometimes only look at a few things in a room?
questions.expl: [AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Daniel: "I sometimes walk into a room and choose just five things to look at."

questions.text: Who learns more in a museum than in a classroom?
questions.expl: [AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Chris: "I've actually found out a lot more about them from museums than from my textbooks."

questions.expl: [AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Daniel: "I learn so much more from listening to the person showing us round than I do if I'm by myself."

sections.title: Part 3
sections.instr:
Questions 14-18
For each question, choose the correct answer.
sections.passage:
How I spend my free time
Jay Portman describes his unusual hobby, hill running, and tells us why he enjoys it.

Hill running is the sport of running up and down hills and mountains, through open countryside. It's not popular among my friends, but I love it. My dad took me and my brothers out running when we were little, and then when I was about fifteen, I joined a hill running club, called the York Merlins.

There are some excellent runners in the club. When we do our practice runs, I'm always a long way behind them. But that doesn't bother me. They're all really nice and often give me advice. What I love is being outdoors and finding all these beautiful places I never knew were there.

We race against other clubs at the weekends. In these races, runners are told where to finish, but not how to get there. You need a good map and compass so you don't get lost. Everyone starts together at the beginning, but later in the race you often find yourself running alone.

Anyone can enter these races - you just get there in the morning, pay your £5, and run. There are no T-shirts or medals for the winners. The most you get is a piece of cake! Often there are international hill running champions taking part, but they are just as friendly as everyone else.

That doesn't mean it's an easy sport. Last weekend I did a race in heavy rain and high winds, and I was asking myself what I was doing out there. But I got to the end, and that was an amazing feeling.

questions.text: Jay's first experience of hill running was with
questions.expl: [AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Đoạn 1: "My dad took me and my brothers out running when we were little..."

questions.text: How does Jay feel about the good runners in his club?
questions.expl: [AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Đoạn 2: "I'm always a long way behind them. But that doesn't bother me."
opts: He'd like to be as fast as them one day.
He doesn't mind that they are better than him.
He thinks they should help slower runners improve.

questions.text: What does Jay say is important in the races he enters?
questions.expl: [AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Đoạn 3: "runners are told where to finish, but not how to get there. You need a good map and compass so you don't get lost."
opts: being able to find your way

questions.text: What do we learn about the races from the fourth paragraph?
questions.expl: [AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Đoạn 4: "There are no T-shirts or medals for the winners. The most you get is a piece of cake!"
opts: They are only for local runners.
They are free for some people to enter.

questions.text: What does Jay say about the last race he did?
questions.expl: [AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Đoạn 5: "But I got to the end, and that was an amazing feeling."
opts: The bad weather made it dangerous.
He was very happy when he finished it.
It wasn't as difficult as some races he has done.

sections.title: Part 4
sections.instr:
Questions 19-24
For each question, choose the correct answer.
sections.passage:
Dakota Fanning
Dakota Fanning was born on February 23rd 1994, in Georgia, USA. She began acting classes at a very (19) ......... age and starred in her first TV advert when she was just five years old.
After that, she had a long and successful (20) ......... as a child actor in both TV shows and films. In 2001, she (21) ......... an important prize for her part in the film I am Sam. Over the next ten years, she acted with many big Hollywood stars, including Reese Witherspoon, Tom Cruise and Kurt Russell.
Dakota Fanning is different from many child actors because her success continued as she (22) ......... up and became an adult. In 2018, she (23) ......... to TV for the first time in ten years, starring in a popular police drama set in the nineteenth century, (24) ......... The Alienist.

questions.expl: [AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Cụm từ "at an early age" nghĩa là từ khi còn nhỏ.
[AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] "career as a child actor" chỉ sự nghiệp làm diễn viên nhí.
[AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Kết hợp từ "won a prize" (giành giải thưởng).
[AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Động từ phrasal "grew up" (trưởng thành).
[AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] "returned to TV" (quay trở lại truyền hình).
[AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Mang nghĩa "được gọi/tên là" The Alienist.

sections.title: Part 5
sections.instr:
Questions 25-30
For each question, write the correct answer. Write one word for each gap.

sections.passage:
New Message
From: Tom
To: Rob

I'm writing (0) about my party on Saturday. Thanks so (25) ......... for offering to help me get everything ready. (26) ......... don't you come over to my place tomorrow (27) ......... school? We can have dinner together and start planning. (28) ......... are lots of things to think about!
Also, I wanted to (29) ......... you know that I'm going to invite a girl called Hannah to the party. She's just moved into the house next door to mine, so it will (30) ......... a good way for her to meet people and make friends.
Text me if you can come tomorrow.

questions.expl: [AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] "Thanks so much" (Cảm ơn rất nhiều).
[AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Cấu trúc gợi ý "Why don't you...?".
[AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] "after school" (sau giờ học).
[AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] "There are lots of things..." (Có rất nhiều thứ...).
[AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Cụm từ "let you know" (cho bạn biết).
[AI tự giải – cần kiểm tra] Sau động từ khuyết thiếu "will" dùng động từ nguyên mẫu "be".
